findings.F1: In falling calm bars, the coin's past 5-day return predicts its next 5-day return in the same direction (slope 0.17, t 2.62, 342 non-overlapping cases). The lowest third of past 5-day returns is followed by -1.6 %, the middle third by -0.3 % and the highest third by +2.2 %. Inside the tested situation (30-day return below 0) the slope is 0.22 (t 2.68, 254 cases), with thirds at -2.1 %, +0.0 % and +1.9 %.
findings.F2: Outside falling calm, the same 5-day continuation is absent (slope -0.001, t -0.05, 1207 cases), so this short-horizon continuation lives in the falling calm profile.
findings.F3: The brief's own situation does not grade the move: in falling calm, the depth of the 30-day fall has no link with the next 5 days (slope 0.017, t 0.48, 281 cases), nor does the 60-day fall (t -0.26, 209 cases).
findings.F4: Volume does not separate the outcomes. Inside the regime the 30-day-versus-year volume ratio has a slope of -0.006 (t -0.35, 268 cases), and the verdict's heavy-minus-quiet difference is -1.29 % (Welch t -0.98, 58 against 408 cases). The worst cell is shallow falls on quiet volume (-1.7 %, 54 cases), while deep falls return about 0.0 % on both quiet and heavy volume (53 cases each).
findings.F5: The tested idea has no size against its cost. Its unusual move is +0.08 % per 5-day case (t 0.13 over 305 days), 0.017 of a usual move, against a 0.19 % cost per trade. The book has a Sharpe of 0.086 and a yearly return of +0.3 %.
findings.F6: Other angles did not stand out after counting how many were looked at, so no idea is drawn from them:

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, a coin's last 5 days carry on over the next 5 days, and the further it has fallen over its last 5 days, the more it falls over the next 5 days. The further it has risen over those 5 days, the more it rises.
ideas.consequence: In a calm downtrend, a trader would trade the coin in the direction of its past week rather than the depth of its past month, shorting the sharpest recent drops.
ideas.name: calm downtrend weekly continuation
